title: Continuity of Hom out of $a_!L$
statement:
Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme (for instance a standing scheme), $\Lambda$ admissible,
$a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $i$ a closed immersion with
quasi-compact open complement $j\colon V\hookrightarrow X$ and $u$ a quasi-compact open
immersion, and $L$ a finite locally free $\Lambda_S$-module. For a filtered diagram
$(K_i^\bullet)$ of complexes of $\Lambda_X$-modules vanishing in degrees $<b$ with colimit $K$,
the natural map
$$
\varinjlim_i\Hom(a_!L,K_i[q])\to\Hom(a_!L,K[q])
$$
is bijective for every $q$.

proof.text: Closed i and quasi-compact open uS imply that Z and S are qcqs. Use the given quasi-compact complementary open, rather than deriving its quasi-compactness from noetherianity.

Generalize the existing closed-costalk continuity proof to qcqs T with a specified quasi-compact complementary open. Apply the natural recollement triangle to the diagram and its good-truncated colimit cocone. Homology and qcqs open pushforward commute with this colimit. Exact filtered colimits and the five lemma give the closed term, and exact fully faithful closed pushforward reflects its isomorphism. Uniqueness of right adjoints handles the specified exceptional inverse image.

Bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective. Apply the derived comparison and its naturality to the source diagram and cocone vertex. The representative comparison criterion turns derived costalk continuity into a quasi-isomorphism of strict costalk cocones.

Resolve the diagram and its colimit functorially by bounded injective complexes preserving the common strict lower bound. Construct the objectwise injective embedding from the degree-zero part of the existing Grothendieck K-injective resolution. Exact filtered colimits make the resolution cocone a quasi-colimit. Apply closed costalk and exact open restriction; derived adjunction gives compatible Hom diagram and vertex isomorphisms.

Transport the lisse trivializations along the invertible coefficient pullback, using scalar restriction equivalences and regular-module isomorphisms. Internal Hom from a locally finite free module preserves colimits. Its tensor left adjoint is exact, so internal Hom preserves K-injectives. Derived composition, internal-Hom sections and derived coyoneda evaluation identify shifted Hom with derived sections of termwise internal Hom. Qcqs sections continuity proves its comparison invertible. This argument requires no noetherian hypothesis.

Precompose the desired comparison equation with every colimit inclusion. The compatibility identity of the costalk model identifies its composite with the vertex isomorphism with the colimit of the diagram isomorphism followed by the finite-free Hom comparison. Both are invertible, so cancel the vertex isomorphism. This proves the original colimit.post, with its unchanged signature. Rank zero and empty strata are included throughout.

proof_origin.source: Blueprint stratum continuity proof; Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Lemma 5.3(1),(2), and the existing Lean costalk-model argument, generalized to qcqs schemes with a specified quasi-compact open complement.
